summary: Trungram Gyalwa Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Harvard (PhD, 2004). He was a visiting scholar at the University of Michigan and Numata Visiting Professor at McGill (2016).
Tré Khen Zur Lozang Wangchuk was a scholar who studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Trịnh Xuân Thuận works in religious studies and other fields. He studied at the California Institute of Technology (~1967–1970) and Princeton University (~1970–1974), and held a post at the University of Virginia around 1976.

Tse-fu Kuan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford in 2004 under Richard Gombrich. He conducted postdoctoral research at National Cheng Kung University and held a post at Yuan Ze University (attested 2015).

Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1914–1983) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Monastery, earning a Geshe Lharampa degree, and held a post at Ganden Jangtse Monastery. He taught Tenzin Gyatso, Alexander Berzin, and Thubten Chodron.

Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Panjab University, Tibetan Children's Villages, and the University of Glasgow (1987). He served as headmaster at Tibetan Children's Villages and became Instructor in Tibetan at Oxford in 2001.
Tsering Gyaltsen is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and under traditional teacher Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje.

Tsering Shakya works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his BA, MPhil, and PhD (2004) at SOAS, where he was a research fellow (1999–2002). He taught at Oxford and joined the University of British Columbia (~2005).

Tsewang Gyurme is a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as President of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences and as president of the Tibetan Association for Sacred Studies (attested 2006).

Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche (1953–2020) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Young Lamas Home School. He served as master of Vajrayana ceremonies at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling (~1974–2020) and on the board of Rangjung Yeshe Shenpen.

Tso Sze-bong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982) under the doctoral supervision of Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.

Tsoknyi Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Khampagar Monastery and under teachers including Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima. He held a post at Tergar Osel Ling Monastery and founded the Pundarika Foundation.

Tsuguhito Takeuchi (1951–2021) was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, University of Pennsylvania, and Indiana University (PhD, 1980–1994, supervised by Christopher I. Beckwith), later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies (~1994–2017).

Tsugunari Kubo (1936–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University (PhD, 1985). He lectured at Rissho University, served as President of Reiyukai, and founded the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Tsui Lan Liza Cheung is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013) under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti, having also studied under Toshiichi Endo.

Tsukasa Mizushima is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1979–1995) and became professor emeritus at the University of Tokyo (1997–2018).

Tsultrim Gyatso is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He served as a senior instructor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Dratsang (attested 1987).

Tsultrim Kelsang is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held lecturer and professor posts at Otani University (attested 1984–2002), was affiliated with the International Buddhist Association (1973), and held research posts at Ryukoku University and Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center (2015).

Tsuneki Nishiwaki is a scholar in Sinology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tokyo University of Education (1962–1966). He held a post at Doshisha University (~1975–1992) and served as a professor at Kyoto University (~1992–2007).
Tsutomu Hatai (1923–2018) worked in Indology and other fields. Attested in 1987, he succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama and served as president of the Ayurveda Research Society.
